Definition: of Hebrew origin (H4968); Mathusala (i.e. Methushelach), an antediluvian:--Mathusala.
BiblicalUsage: Methuselah's name reaches the New Testament in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, where he stands between Enoch and Lamech, the link back to the man who lived longer than anyone in Scripture. Luke traces Jesus through him to show that the Saviour belongs to the whole line of Adam, not only to Abraham.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the genealogy is the point: Jesus is not a late idea in God's plan, but the heir of the oldest line on earth, and Methuselah's long life is part of the road that leads to Him.
